title: LPG Strategy
definition: The LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation) Strategy refers to the sweeping structural economic reforms introduced in India in July 1991 to dismantle the License-Permit-Quota Raj, resolve the acute Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis, and integrate the domestic economy with the global market.
importanceInUpsc: This microtopic is a foundational pillar of the Indian Economy syllabus for both Prelims (direct policy questions, committees, and reform chronological sequences) and Mains GS-3 (evaluation of economic reforms, inclusive growth, industrial policy, and globalization impacts).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of the 1991 LPG Strategy.
Evaluate spatial distribution, structural changes, and institutional frameworks across different economic sectors.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions on economic reforms.
prerequisites: Macroeconomic indicators (Fiscal Deficit, Inflation, Forex Reserves)
